sciXsTrack: Which ramp makes a toy car go the slowest?
A ramp as steep as a slide
A gentle ramp gives the car less speed than a steep one.
Your toy car crashes hard at the bottom of the ramp. What could slow it down safely?
Put a soft towel at the end
A soft towel adds friction and cushions the car so it stops gently.
Which surface slows a toy car down the most?
Thick carpet has a lot of friction, so it slows the car the most.
Your track has a big gap in it. What should you do?
Fill the gap with another piece of track
Filling the gap lets the car keep rolling without falling.
What is a good first step before you build a race car track?
Draw a plan of the track
Engineers plan their design before they build it.
You want to know which of two cars is faster. How can you make the race fair?
Race both cars on the same ramp
Use a steeper ramp for one car
Using the same ramp for both cars means only the cars are different.
A track that lets a car go around and come back to the start is shaped like a…
A loop goes around and returns to where it started.
What could you use to build a ramp for a toy car?
Cardboard is flat and stiff, so a car can roll down it.
What happens when a toy car starts from higher up on a ramp?
Starting higher gives the car more speed as it rolls down.
Your car stops in the middle of the track. How can you help it go all the way?
Start it from higher on the ramp
A higher start gives the car more speed so it rolls farther.
Which kind of wheels helps a toy car roll best on a track?
Wheels glued so they cannot turn
Round wheels that spin freely let the car roll easily.
Your car flies off the track at a sharp turn. What could you change?
Make the turn wider and gentler
Take away the sides of the track
A wider, gentler turn helps the car stay on the track.
How can you tell which car rolled the farthest?
Guess by looking at the colours
Measuring the distance gives a fair answer.
One track is smooth and one is bumpy. On which track will a car slow down more?
Bumps create more friction and slow the car down.
What could you use to hold up one end of a ramp?
A stack of books is strong and steady enough to raise a ramp.
Your friend's track design works better than yours. What should you do?
Look at their design and try their ideas
Engineers learn from other designs to improve their own.
Why should you test your track more than one time?
To check that the result is the same each time
Testing many times shows whether the results can be trusted.
Which part of a track could make a toy car jump?
A small ramp that tilts up at the end
A ramp that tilts up launches the car into the air.
Which tool helps you time a toy car race?
A stopwatch measures how long the car takes to finish.
Your ramp keeps sliding when the car rolls down. How can you fix it?
Tape the ramp so it stays in place
Tape holds the ramp steady so it does not slide.
Which track would make a toy car go the fastest?
Steepness adds speed and smoothness means less friction.
Your toy car keeps tipping over on the track. What could help?
Make the track wider and flatter
A wide, flat track gives the car a steady path.

sciXsETrans: A battery-powered fan changes chemical energy into…
The battery's chemical energy becomes electricity, which spins the fan's motor.
An electric kettle changes electrical energy into…
The kettle's heating element turns electricity into heat that boils the water.
A microphone changes sound energy into…
A microphone turns sound vibrations into electrical signals.
A campfire changes the chemical energy in wood into…
Burning wood releases stored chemical energy as heat and light.
An electric motor changes electrical energy into…
A motor uses electricity to make something spin or move.
A hydroelectric dam changes the kinetic energy of falling water into…
Falling water spins turbines connected to generators that make electricity.
A doorbell changes electrical energy into…
Pressing the button sends electricity to the bell, which makes sound.
A battery being charged changes electrical energy into…
Charging stores energy in the battery as chemical energy.
A glow stick changes chemical energy into…
Chemicals inside a glow stick react and give off light.
A hand-crank flashlight changes kinetic energy into…
Turning the crank spins a generator, and the electricity powers the bulb.
A drum changes the kinetic energy of the drumstick into…
Hitting the drum makes it vibrate, which produces sound.
A ball held high and then dropped changes gravitational potential energy into…
As the ball falls, its stored energy of height turns into motion.
An electric stove changes electrical energy into…
The stove's burners turn electricity into heat for cooking.
A stretched elastic band changes elastic potential energy into…
kinetic energy when it is let go
The stored energy in the stretched band turns into motion when released.
A television changes electrical energy into…
A TV uses electricity to make pictures (light) and sound.
A bicycle's brakes change kinetic energy into…
Friction between brake pads and the wheel turns motion into heat.
A natural gas furnace changes chemical energy into…
Burning natural gas releases heat that warms a home.
A firefly changes chemical energy into…
Chemical reactions in a firefly's body produce light.
A swinging pendulum keeps changing energy between…
At the top it has the most potential energy, and at the bottom it has the most kinetic energy.
A roller coaster going down a hill changes potential energy into…
As the car drops, its stored energy of height becomes speed.
A phone's speaker changes electrical energy into…
The speaker uses electricity to vibrate and make sound.
When you lift a backpack onto a shelf, your muscles change chemical energy into…
kinetic energy and then gravitational potential energy
Your muscles use food energy to move the backpack, which gains stored energy from its height.
